items.prompt:
CPython 3.12.13: run source, then call. What returns/raises (exact types/value/order)?

def f(x):
 a=[[1,2],[3,4]]
 b=a[:]
 a[0].append(x)
 a[1]=[5]
 return b

Call:
f(*[9], **{})

goal.title: Prepare for Python interviews by understanding program behavior
goal.focusAreas: Interpret reference sharing and control flow instead of memorizing outputs

sourceDocuments.name: Python assignment and shallow copying
sourceDocuments.text: Assignment binds names to objects. A shallow copy recreates the outer container while preserving references to its members. A whole-list slice is a shallow copy.

sourceDocuments.name: Python loop control
sourceDocuments.text: Loop else runs after normal completion. A break, return or raised exception skips it. Break exits the innermost enclosing loop; continue advances that loop.

goal.title: Understand HTML form behavior when states and constraints interact
goal.focusAreas: Predict native form-control state from the actual ancestor structure and attributes

sourceDocuments.name: HTML disabled controls and validation
sourceDocuments.text: A disabled fieldset disables descendant controls except descendants of its first legend child. Disabled controls are barred from constraint validation. willValidate reflects validation candidacy. checkValidity() returns false only for a candidate that fails its constraints; otherwise it returns true.
